unit.title: Guru Gobind Singh Ji and the Panj Pyare

contentBlocks.text: Last week you learned about Vaisakhi and the Khalsa. Today, meet the Guru who founded it: Guru Gobind Singh Ji!

Guru Gobind Singh Ji was born in a city called Patna, and he became Guru when he was still a child. Even though he was young, he grew up to be a courageous, caring leader who founded the Khalsa at Vaisakhi in 1699 — the same event you learned about last week. What is one word you would use to describe a leader who became Guru while still a child?
You just met Guru Gobind Singh Ji, the founder of the Khalsa! Tomorrow we'll meet the five brave people who joined him first.

objectives: Identify Guru Gobind Singh Ji as the Guru who founded the Khalsa
Recall that he was born in Patna and became Guru at a young age
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's Vaisakhi/Khalsa-founding story briefly.
2. Introduce Guru Gobind Singh Ji: born in Patna, became Guru young, founded the Khalsa.
3. Discuss the child's own word for a young leader.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's Panj Pyare lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the single connection — 'Guru Gobind Singh Ji founded the Khalsa you learned about last week' — as the core takeaway
Ready for more: ask the child what qualities they think a good leader needs, connecting back to Guru Gobind Singh Ji
Text-only, per the platform's Ten Gurus content policy — no illustration or depiction of Guru Gobind Singh Ji
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a recall and reflection activity — check that the child can state that Guru Gobind Singh Ji founded the Khalsa and became Guru at a young age.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly extends the course's 'story of Vaisakhi' description by introducing its central figure, deepening last week's introduction without repeating it.
